intro: The club’s founder kept a letterpress type case in the trophy room, and the senior players still treat the odd sheets as sorts: every compartment has a place of exactly the right depth, and a piece dropped into the wrong one wobbles or leaves a gap. When the champion who resigned in a won position left the hall and never played again, his scoresheet was not put among the recorded games; it was laid across the case and then, after a long silence, slid into the one compartment that took it flush. The backing papers in the case are thin sheets of laid paper, and in every row one backing has been stained amber where the rest are cream. Apprentices are told that the case does not care about the beauty of a move, only about whether a sort belongs where it sits, and that the stained backs are the part to watch when the sorting is done. The sheet that was not a game at all has been waiting there since the ink was still wet.
echo: Every good opening starts by giving something away.

puzzles.title: Queen's Gambit
puzzles.flavor: Find them all. The letters nobody used are the only ones that were talking to you.

blocks.text: Hidden in the grid: 11 words to do with the tournament hall (lengths 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6, 7, 7), running in any direction.

hints: Find every hidden word (any of 8 directions). The unused letters, read left-to-right, top-to-bottom, spell the answer.
The hidden words are: ARBITER, CHECK, CLOCK, ENDGAME, FILE, FORK, FRENCH, PAWN, QUEEN, RANK, ROOK.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with G.

puzzles.title: Opposition
puzzles.flavor: The spy's handbook said to always carry a novel. It never said which one; this page will have to do.

blocks.text: A grandmaster resigned in a winning position, left the hall, and never played again. His scoresheet was not a game at all.

hints: Each pair is word.letter into the recovered page (words split on spaces; punctuation ignored).
To check you're on track: the answer begins with S.

puzzles.title: Time Trouble
puzzles.flavor: Someone on the pier is trying very hard to get your attention.
hints: Flag semaphore: read each figure's arm positions.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with B.

puzzles.title: Adjournment
puzzles.flavor: Somebody shook the sentence and all the letters fell to the bottom of their columns.
hints: A drop quote: each column's letters (shown alphabetised above it) drop into that column of the grid below. Black squares are spaces; words can wrap between rows. The sentence tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with K.

puzzles.title: Smothered Mate
puzzles.flavor: Every letter here is wearing someone else's coat. The spaces, at least, are honest.

blocks.text: GMGHW QCCS UOID GISE AVDU Y EVIQNG ACHS YIS DUG ACHS WCO AYID THCZ DUVE XYQG VE KYDYNYI

hints: Simple monoalphabetic substitution with word breaks kept. Solve the sentence; it tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with C.

puzzles.title: Fianchetto
puzzles.flavor: Three letters to a strip. The strips are in order; the sentence isn't.
hints: The sentence was cut into three-letter fragments (spaces removed) and alphabetised. Reassemble it using the word lengths; it tells you the answer.
To check you're on track: the answer begins with B.

meta.title: Meta: The Endgame Study
meta.flavor: Everything in the tournament hall has a place, and every place is exactly the right size.
hints: Each answer fits exactly one row of the grid by length; the shaded squares, top to bottom, spell the final answer.
To check you're on track: the final answer begins with G.
